claims.claim: **This page covers gynaecological causes only** — other causes of acute abdominal pain must also be considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Obstetric emergencies** (ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, placental abruption, uterine rupture) **and gynaecological emergencies** (ovarian or adnexal torsion) **need urgent gynaecological or surgical referral.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Torsion is a clinical diagnosis; do not delay gynaecological referral for investigations such as ultrasound.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Menstrual history:** menarche, LMP, cycle frequency, duration, flow, pain, flooding, **clots larger than 2 cm**, pad/tampon change frequency.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also ask** about vaginal discharge, pain characteristics (sudden onset, quality, severity, triggers, bowel/bladder symptoms, fever, vomiting), sexual history and contraception, systemic features, and a HEADSS screen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-specific episodic pain:** consider constipation, abdominal migraine and functional abdominal pain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Examine for pallor, hypotension, tachycardia and an abdominal (uterine or ovarian) mass.** **Vaginal examination is rarely indicated** — discuss with a senior clinician and perform it only once.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ovarian or adnexal torsion:** sharp pelvic pain of acute, sudden onset — generalised or one-sided (usually right lower quadrant), possibly intermittent; adnexal mass; nausea and vomiting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ectopic pregnancy:** abdominal/pelvic pain, missed period then vaginal bleeding, possible shoulder-tip pain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Acute placental abruption:** back and/or abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, contractions and DIC in severe cases; any gestation, peak 24–26 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Uterine rupture:** peritonism, uterine tenderness, abnormal fetal heart rate, vaginal bleeding. **Molar pregnancy:** severe vomiting, an enlarged uterus, pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PID:** risk factors (e.g. unprotected sex), mucopurulent discharge, post-coital bleeding, fever, pelvic or lower abdominal pain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mittelschmerz:** mild unilateral recurrent midcycle pain. **Ruptured ovarian cyst:** one-sided pelvic pain, severe and sudden, sometimes after strenuous activity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Endometriosis:** crampy pelvic pain with menses, possibly with pain on defecation, urination or intercourse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imperforate hymen:** amenorrhoea, cyclical pain, vaginal distension causing back pain or pain on defecation or urination. **Retained foreign body:** discharge, intermittent bleeding or spotting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do a βhCG (with consent)** — urine, and/or blood if a quantitative result is needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Critical cause suspected: pelvic ultrasound**, transabdominal (full bladder) or transvaginal (sexually active, with consent) — but never delaying torsion referral.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infection suspected:** urine MCS; first-pass urine NAAT for *Chlamydia trachomatis* and *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*, or a vaginal/endocervical swab (MCS, chlamydia, gonorrhoea); FBE, CRP ± blood culture if PID or sepsis is a real concern.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for haemodynamic instability, marked pain or unclear cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgent gynaecology (or surgical) consultation** for suspected torsion, ectopic pregnancy, threatened miscarriage or non-viable pregnancy; also for causes needing surgery, and PID.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when stable with a GP review scheduled.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23
